title: STM32 in Practice: From One LED to a System You Can Ship
subtitle: A 29-chapter evidence-driven introduction and engineering handbook
keywords: STM32, Cortex-M, embedded systems, FreeRTOS, RT-Thread, Zephyr, CMSIS-RTOS2, lwIP, Ethernet, MQTT, TLS
author: zhuguang-ZFG and contributors

license.third_party_images: CC0 1.0 (only the assets/photos items that are labeled)

parts.title: Part 1  Start: a development loop you can repeat
parts.goal: Write the learning route, the toolchain, the chip boundary, and the clock assumptions down as an engineering record you can reproduce.

parts.title: Part 2  GPIO, interrupts, and time
parts.goal: Go from one pin to asynchronous events and a hardware time base, and prove the configuration with a waveform instead of guessing by eye.

parts.title: Part 3  Serial buses, sampling, and DMA
parts.goal: Reconcile level, frame, buffer, and memory consistency, and explain where every byte comes from and where it goes.

parts.title: Part 4  Reliability, links, scheduling, and debug
parts.goal: Put power loss, updates, networks, USB, real-time scheduling, low power, and fault finding inside one engineering boundary.

parts.title: Part 5  Delivery: troubleshooting, projects, sources, and simulation
parts.goal: Turn scattered peripherals into a project you can reproduce, and state the limits of the document layers, the board evidence, and the simulation model.

parts.title: Part 6  Migration, legacy projects, and networks
parts.goal: Migrate by package, supply, clock, memory, cache, and network layer; keep a legacy SPL project maintainable; and put the device on a network you can diagnose, recover, and authenticate.

parts.title: Part 7  System architecture: from kernel objects to a product you can ship
parts.goal: Put scheduling, devices, services, faults, and the resource budget on one system diagram, and choose FreeRTOS, RT-Thread, Zephyr, or bare metal against those constraints.

00-how-to-learn-stm32.md.question: How does a beginner build a learning path that is not drowned by tools, jargon, and the number of tutorials?
00-how-to-learn-stm32.md.deliverable: A personal learning route, a minimum hardware list, and a first blink record of expected versus measured values.
00-how-to-learn-stm32.md.boundary: This chapter only sets the order of entry. It does not replace C, electrical safety, or the target chip manual.

01-dev-environment.md.question: How does source become machine state you can single-step, after compile, link, flash, and reset?
01-dev-environment.md.deliverable: A minimal project that rebuilds, downloads, and hits a breakpoint, with the IDE, compiler, firmware package, and board versions recorded.
01-dev-environment.md.boundary: A working toolchain does not mean the peripherals are configured correctly. Clock, pins, and electrical conditions still need to be checked one by one.

02-part-and-clock.md.question: How do the part number, the memory map, and the clock tree together decide whether a program can run on the target chip?
02-part-and-clock.md.deliverable: A breakdown of the target part, a Flash/SRAM address map, and a SYSCLK/APB/timer clock ledger.
02-part-and-clock.md.boundary: The examples are mainly F103. Any production choice must go back to the exact order code, revision, and temperature grade. The BluePill example is an STM32F103C8T6 in LQFP48: an 8 MHz HSE times 9 is 72 MHz, and the Flash wait for 48–72 MHz is 2. Check the kilobytes at 0x1FFFF7E0 against the 64 KB in DS5319.

03-gpio-and-led.md.question: How do a pin's input structure, output drive, and external load together decide the real level?
03-gpio-and-led.md.deliverable: A pin-mode, wiring, and expected-level table, with both output states checked on a meter or a logic analyzer.
03-gpio-and-led.md.boundary: A GPIO mode does not change the absolute maximum ratings. 5 V tolerance and sink/source current must be checked for the specific pin. On the BluePill, PC13's LED is on when the pin is low. An F1 internal pull-up is about 30–50 kΩ and does not replace an I2C resistor.

04-interrupts-nvic.md.question: How does an asynchronous event travel from a pin through EXTI and the NVIC, and how does the ISR exit safely in a bounded time?
04-interrupts-nvic.md.deliverable: An event-path diagram, a priority table, and a worst-case ISR execution-time budget.
04-interrupts-nvic.md.boundary: A bare-metal priority setup does not automatically meet an RTOS FromISR constraint. Chapter 15 adds the kernel boundary. Hardware stacking saves 8 registers in about 12 HCLK cycles; at 72 MHz that is about 167 ns, and the ISR body is extra. HAL's default grouping is GROUP_4: 4 preemption bits and 0 subpriority bits. A smaller number is a higher logical priority.

05-timer-pwm.md.question: How do the clock, PSC, ARR, and CCR become a measurable period, frequency, and duty cycle?
05-timer-pwm.md.deliverable: A calculation from the timer input clock to the target waveform, and a table of instrument measurements beside it.
05-timer-pwm.md.boundary: The formula holds only for the chosen count mode and clock path. An advanced timer also needs MOE, dead time, and complementary outputs checked. On this F103, when APB1 is 36 MHz, TIM2–TIM7 still count at 72 MHz. With PSC 71 and ARR 999, 72 MHz / (72 × 1000) = 1 kHz. The same PSC and ARR divided by 36 MHz produce 500 Hz. A 16-bit timer cannot hold ARR 999999.

06-uart.md.question: How do UART bit timing, error flags, the DMA buffer, and the frame boundary become a reliable receive path?
06-uart.md.deliverable: An 8N1 waveform, a handling table for ORE/FE/NE, and a receive scheme whose buffer invariant is written down.
06-uart.md.boundary: IDLE only means the line is idle. It is not one frame of an application protocol. In circular DMA, Size is the write position, not the increment of this transfer. USART1 is on APB2: at 115200, 72 MHz, and 16× oversampling, BRR is 0x271 and the divider error is 0. One bit is about 8.68 µs, so an 8N1 frame is about 86.8 µs.

07-i2c.md.question: How do open-drain electricals, pull-up time, and START/ACK/repeated start together decide one I2C transaction?
07-i2c.md.deliverable: A wiring and address table, one logic-analyzer decode, and a recovery record after the bus is held low.
07-i2c.md.boundary: Seeing an address only proves a device ACKed. It does not prove the register protocol, the supply, or the data meaning. The SSD1306 7-bit address 0x3C is 0x78 in HAL. A short bus wants 4.7 kΩ; the on-chip pull-up, about 30–50 kΩ, will not carry 400 kHz.

08-spi.md.question: How do CPOL, CPHA, chip select, and full-duplex shifting decide when each bit is driven and sampled?
08-spi.md.deliverable: A comparison of the target device's timing with the MCU mode, and a read-back of a read-only register with a known reset value.
08-spi.md.boundary: A value that is not all 0s or all 1s does not prove the mode is correct. It must match the device manual's ID or reset value. SPI1 is on APB2. At 72 MHz, BR 010 divides by 8 and SCK is 9 MHz; BR 001 is 18 MHz. The only dividers are 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, and 256. The JEDEC command is 0x9F. This repository's spi-flash example expects manufacturer 0xEF, memory type 0x40, and capacity 0x17. The page is 256 bytes. Mode 0 is CPOL 0 and CPHA 0.

09-adc-dac.md.question: How do source impedance, sample-and-hold, the reference, and quantization together decide an ADC code?
09-adc-dac.md.deliverable: An error chain from input voltage to code and back to voltage, with endpoint, midpoint, and internal-reference readings recorded.
09-adc-dac.md.boundary: The example formula uses a nominal reference. A precision claim must include VDDA, calibration, sample time, and the exact part. With PCLK2 at 72 MHz, the F103 ADC prescaler is ÷6, which is 12 MHz, and must not exceed 14 MHz.

10-dma.md.question: How do you check, separately, the DMA request, reachable memory, transfer width, ring position, and cache coherence?
10-dma.md.deliverable: A request map, a buffer ownership and placement invariant, and an H7 decision on memory reachability and cache maintenance.
10-dma.md.boundary: A DMA-complete interrupt only proves the controller finished the request. It does not prove the CPU read the latest data, or that the application dropped no frame. An F103C8 has only DMA1, seven channels, and no DMA2. USART1_TX is channel 4, USART1_RX is channel 5, and ADC1 is channel 1. Eight half-words with CNDTR reading 3 means 5 samples have been written, which is 10 bytes. Half-transfer is half the item count, not half the byte count. On F4, USART1_RX is DMA2 stream 5, channel 4. The FIFO is four 32-bit words.

11-rtc-watchdog.md.question: How does time survive loss of the main supply, and how does a watchdog prove the main loop is actually healthy rather than merely being fed?
11-rtc-watchdog.md.deliverable: A power-loss timekeeping record, a reset-reason record after a deliberate missed feed, and an explicit healthy-feed condition.
11-rtc-watchdog.md.boundary: A watchdog reset is not itself a fault-recovery strategy. State persistence, fault counts, and safe degradation still need a system design. A nominal 1 second is prescaler 64 and Reload 624, taking LSI as 40 kHz. The manual range is about 30–60 kHz, so that second is not a guarantee.

12-flash-iap.md.question: How do you hand a new firmware image to the application safely, under erase limits, address boundaries, and power-loss risk?
12-flash-iap.md.deliverable: A Boot/APP memory map, an image-integrity check, and a state diagram for falling back when an update fails.
12-flash-iap.md.boundary: Being able to jump to the application is not a production update. Signature, anti-rollback, power-loss recovery, and key management need their own argument. A medium-density F103 erases 1 KB pages and programs half-words. Unlock writes KEY1 0x45670123, then KEY2 0xCDEF89AB. High-density pages are 2 KB. An F407 sector is 16 KB, 64 KB, or 128 KB.

13-can.md.question: How do physical termination, bit timing, arbitration, filters, and error counters together decide whether a CAN frame can be trusted?
13-can.md.deliverable: A bit-timing ledger, a loopback self-test, and a captured frame from two nodes with termination resistors.
13-can.md.boundary: This chapter covers bxCAN basics. It is not CANopen or J1939, and H7 FDCAN registers cannot be substituted as-is. With APB1 at 36 MHz, prescaler 9, BS1 5, and BS2 2 give 8 time quanta, a 75% sample point, and 36 MHz / (9 × 8) = 500 kbit/s. Ten quanta at the same target need a prescaler of 7.2; writing 8 yields 450 kbit/s. A transmit error count of 256 enters bus-off.

14-usb.md.question: How does the host finish enumeration through reset, descriptors, address, and configuration, and where does the class protocol take over the data?
14-usb.md.deliverable: An enumeration request sequence, a full descriptor-length check, and a host-visible result for CDC or HID.
14-usb.md.boundary: Successful enumeration only proves the control transfers are basically correct. Throughput, compatibility, suspend/resume, and compliance still need their own tests. F103 full-speed needs 48 MHz: with the PLL at 72 MHz, RCC_CFGR.USBPRE is 0, and 72 / 1.5 = 48. PA11 is DM and PA12 is DP. Full-speed pulls D+ up with 1.5 kΩ. This repository's usb-cdc device descriptor is 18 bytes, bMaxPacketSize0 is 64, and the VID/PID is 0x1209/0x0001, not the 0x0483/0x5740 common in ST's examples. wTotalLength is 0x0043, which is 67 bytes. bMaxPower 0x32 means 100 mA. Full-speed bulk and interrupt both top out at 64 bytes. 1023 belongs only to full-speed isochronous.

15-freertos.md.question: How do tasks, queues, mutexes, and ISRs cooperate under the priority rules without blocking the wrong execution context?
15-freertos.md.deliverable: A task-state diagram, a stack and queue budget, and an NVIC table that shows the FromISR priority is legal.
15-freertos.md.boundary: The example only establishes the kernel's basic contract. Real-time behavior must be shown with worst-case execution time, the blocking chain, and measurements. FreeRTOS requires GROUP_4. With 4 priority bits, 5 << (8-4) = 0x50, so an interrupt that calls FromISR needs a numeric priority of at least 5. NVIC priority 0 is the highest; calling those APIs stops in configASSERT. Task priority runs in the opposite direction. The stack depth passed to xTaskCreate is in words. In this repository's freertos-task example the LED task is 128 words, which is 512 bytes; KEY is 192 words, 768 bytes; UART is 256 words, 1024 bytes. The default configTICK_RATE_HZ is 1000, so one tick is 1 ms. HAL_Delay also uses SysTick. When the kernel is on, move the HAL time base to another timer.

16-low-power.md.question: When entering and leaving Sleep, Stop, or Standby, which clocks, state, and wake sources must be restored explicitly?
16-low-power.md.deliverable: A mode, wake, and retained-state table, and a current measurement that records board load, instrument bandwidth, and temperature.
16-low-power.md.boundary: A typical value in the datasheet is the chip under stated conditions. It is not the power of the whole board. On an F103 the Stop typical is about 14 to 20 µA. Wake-up returns to HSI. Chapter 02 puts that HSI at 8 MHz on F1; the 72 MHz PLL has to be programmed again.

17-debug.md.question: Faced with a crash or a slowdown, how do you go from a repeatable symptom to the fault registers, the call site, and cycle evidence?
17-debug.md.deliverable: A minimal reproduction, a record of CFSR/HFSR/BFAR/MMFAR and the stack, and one DWT comparison before and after an optimization.
17-debug.md.boundary: The optimizer, the debugger, and logging all change timing. A speedup without a baseline and a retest under the same conditions is not evidence. CFSR is at 0xE000ED28, HFSR at 0xE000ED2C, MMFAR at 0xE000ED34, and BFAR at 0xE000ED38. HFSR.FORCED is bit 30, value 0x40000000. BFAR is valid only when bit 15 of CFSR (BFARVALID) is 1. On F103, SWO is PB3. At 72 MHz, 72 DWT cycles are 1 µs. M3 and M4 have 6 hardware breakpoint comparators; M7 has 8.

18-faq.md.question: How do you split "it does not work" into something you can observe, bisect, and change one cause at a time?
18-faq.md.deliverable: A record of expected, actual, and the first point they diverge, plus a minimal project that reproduces the problem on its own.
18-faq.md.boundary: The FAQ is an index, not a patch library. The same symptom can have several root causes, and the evidence has to come from this machine.

19-projects.md.question: How do you cut a multi-peripheral project into milestones you can accept one at a time, instead of integrating every uncertainty at once?
19-projects.md.deliverable: A project boundary, module interfaces, a visible result for each stage, a fallback point, and a reproduction note.
19-projects.md.boundary: The project list is a learning path. It is not a claim of safety, EMC, production test, or regulatory compliance.

20-resources.md.question: When the question is a parameter, a register, the core, an application, or a tool, how do you pick the right document layer and freeze the version?
20-resources.md.deliverable: An environment list with document number and revision, firmware-package tag or commit, compiler, and the board silkscreen.
20-resources.md.boundary: Community answers are for finding a lead. A conclusion that changes product behavior must go back to primary material for that version, and to a measurement.

21-board-maps.md.question: How do you confirm supply, reset, boot, clock, debug, and peripheral wiring from the schematic, instead of trusting the silkscreen?
21-board-maps.md.deliverable: An annotated minimum-system drawing of the board in hand, and a pre-power checklist for supply, ground, and the debug port.
21-board-maps.md.boundary: The board drawings in this book are reading diagrams drawn from the material. They are not manufacturing files, official photographs, or schematics you can send to fabrication.

22-simulation-wokwi-renode.md.question: Which behavior can you watch in Wokwi or Renode, and which conclusions must go back to a real board and instruments?
22-simulation-wokwi-renode.md.deliverable: One visible GPIO result, one USART byte result, and a boundary table of what the model supports, does not support, and leaves unknown.
22-simulation-wokwi-renode.md.boundary: Passing in simulation does not prove analog behavior, the DMA model, timing margin, power, or board-level signal integrity.

23-stm32g0-pins.md.question: When moving from F1 to G071RB, which package pin order, shared BOOT/SWCLK pin, option bytes, and peripheral set must not be copied across?
23-stm32g0-pins.md.deliverable: A critical-pin table for G071RB LQFP64, a diagram of the boot latch and protection branches, a complete boot truth table, and a recovery loop that judges reachability from RDP/DBG_SWEN and reads it back.
23-stm32g0-pins.md.boundary: This chapter answers only for the stated G071RB package and the manual revisions it cites. The empty-Flash check, RDP, DBG_SWEN, the bootloader pattern, and production option bytes must be checked separately. Under Reset does not guarantee a connection. Clearing BOOT_LOCK is limited by RDP. This chapter does not assume an RDP downgrade or a full erase. The family maximum is 64 MHz, on a Cortex-M0+. Boot configuration is latched on the fourth rising edge of SYSCLK. PA14 is both the boot input and SWCLK. When BOOT_LOCK is 1 and RDP is level 1, FLASH_ACR.DBG_SWEN resets to 0.

24-stm32l4-pins.md.question: How do the L476RG pins, power domains, and low-power modes affect entering Stop 2, recovering after wake, and the real average current?
24-stm32l4-pins.md.deliverable: A critical-pin table for LQFP64, a wake evidence chain captured at the IRQ entry before HAL clears the bits, a Stop 2 clock-recovery chain you can verify, and a power ledger with the wiring, the raw waveform, and the integration formula.
24-stm32l4-pins.md.boundary: The raw wake bits must be captured before the HAL handler. A typical low-power number is not a whole-board guarantee. Mode capability, chip revision, VDD, temperature, instrument bandwidth, burden voltage, and board load must be recorded with the result. The cover's Stop 2 typicals are 1.1 µA, 1.4 µA with the RTC, and 4 µs to wake from Stop. Those are the chip under the stated conditions, and they are not a measurement from this repository. The temporary clock after wake-up is MSI or HSI16. A running SysTick wakes the core every 1 ms. Read ES0250 for that revision before turning 1.1 µA into a limit.

25-stm32h7-pins.md.question: After moving to H743ZI, how do the supply scheme, silicon revision, VCAP, FDCAN, cache, and the 400/480 MHz clock tree change the assumptions of an older project?
25-stm32h7-pins.md.deliverable: A critical-pin table for LQFP144, a 400/480 MHz configuration chain that matches the board supply and the revision, and three kinds of acceptance evidence: MCO, a frequency read-back, and a peripheral waveform. DMA buffers keep the memory-domain, alignment, and cache policy from chapter 10.
25-stm32h7-pins.md.boundary: Rev Y and W have no VOS0 and top out at 400 MHz. The 480 MHz example applies only to Rev V, 8 MHz HSE bypass, and a matching LDO board. A supply macro does not replace the schematic. The MCO number is a calculated expectation, not a measurement from this repository. Other peripheral kernel clocks, the MPU, and the DMA memory layout still need their own acceptance. With 8 MHz bypass, PLLM=4, PLLN=400, and PLLP=2, SYSCLK is 400 MHz, and the official example passes Flash wait 4. PLLN=480 belongs only to Rev V, after VOS1 has reported ready and VOS0 is then requested. MCO2 divided by 5 expects 80 MHz at 400 MHz and 96 MHz at 480 MHz.

26-spl.md.question: Faced with an old STM32F10x SPL project, how do you confirm the version, recover the project skeleton, read the API, and move to HAL or LL safely?
26-spl.md.deliverable: A project list locked to V3.5.0, a HAL/SPL/register map, and a waveform comparison that moves only one peripheral at a time.
26-spl.md.boundary: This chapter covers only STM32F10x SPL V3.5.0. It does not treat the old F1 API as the recommended driver for G0, L4, or H7, and it does not authorize initializing the same peripheral from both SPL and HAL.

27-network.md.question: How does an STM32 go from PHY/RMII and DMA/cache to lwIP, TCP/UDP, and MQTT/TLS, and recover in a way you can diagnose after the link drops?
27-network.md.deliverable: A layered data-path diagram, a network debug ladder, a TCP protocol with a length field and an application sequence number, and a fault-injection record covering DHCP, DNS, MQTT, and TLS.
27-network.md.boundary: Link, ping, a TCP ACK, MQTT QoS, and data committed to storage are different evidence layers. H7 DMA memory domain and cache, the lwIP thread context, certificate time, and application idempotence must each be accepted on their own. RMII REF_CLK is 50 MHz. Ethernet DMA cannot reach DTCM at 0x20000000, and buffers are aligned to 32 bytes. DHCP uses UDP 67 (server) and 68 (client). DNS uses port 53. With no IPv4 options and an Ethernet MTU of 1500, the TCP MSS ceiling is 1500 − 20 − 20 = 1460. A smaller MSS in the peer's SYN wins. These numbers do not stand in for each other.

28-system-rtos.md.question: How do you connect the kernel, drivers, system services, and the product state machine into one system with ownership, deadlines, a resource budget, and recovery evidence?
28-system-rtos.md.deliverable: A system layer diagram, a task/interrupt/IPC/memory budget, an OS selection table, and a fault-injection record covering a full queue, a frozen task, and a driver timeout.
28-system-rtos.md.boundary: The API names of FreeRTOS, RT-Thread, Zephyr, and CMSIS-RTOS2 do not replace the target version, the BSP, the execution context, or a worst-case latency check. The example budget is not a hardware measurement. The worked example on this page is 80 µs/1 ms = 8%, 420 µs/10 ms = 4.2%, 70 µs/2 ms = 3.5%, 1.5 ms/100 ms = 1.5%, and 17.2% together. That only says these four items do not fill one core.

rm0008-tim.license: ST document terms (link and restated facts only; the manual is not redistributed)
rm0008-tim.scope: Chapter 05 principle, timing, and source cards. PSC = 71 and ARR = 999 at a 72 MHz counter clock is 1000 Hz. The same numbers divided by 36 MHz are 500 Hz.
